overview: This paper introduces DriftLite, a lightweight, training-free inference-time scaling method for diffusion models that stabilizes particle-based sampling by actively controlling the drift to minimize weight degeneracy, featuring VCG and ECG algorithms to solve for optimal control, and validated on Gaussian mixtures, molecular systems, and protein-ligand co-folding.

modules.name: Base Diffusion EDM Backbone
modules.description: Implements the Elucidating the Design Space (EDM) framework for diffusion models, handling noise level scheduling, network preconditioning (input/output scaling, skip connections), and the conversion between the denoiser output and the score function required for backward sampling.

modules.name: Equivariant Score Network Architecture
modules.description: Constructs the E(n)-Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) used to approximate the score function for particle systems, implementing equivariant graph convolutional layers with attention mechanisms and residual connections to ensure coordinate translation and rotation invariance.

modules.name: Data Generation & Ground Truth Sampling
modules.description: Handles the generation and preprocessing of datasets, including Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) sampling, molecular system initialization, and the simulation of ground-truth reference samples using underdamped Langevin dynamics with the BAOAB splitting scheme for particle systems.

modules.name: Target Distribution & Reward Paths
modules.description: Defines the inference-time scaling tasks by constructing the target distributions, implementing annealing paths (tilting the base distribution by a factor), reward-tilting paths (incorporating quadratic or physics-based rewards), and interpolation schedules for the reward function over time.

modules.name: Guidance Dynamics & Reweighting Potential
modules.description: Implements the Guidance-Based Dynamics from Proposition 2.1, calculating the modified guidance drift and the uncentered reweighting potential which involves derivatives of the reward, score, and forward drift, as well as centering the potential to ensure zero expectation.

modules.name: Drift Control Degree of Freedom
modules.description: Implements the theoretical foundation from Proposition 3.1, providing the mechanism to introduce a control drift into the Fokker-Planck equation and computing the resulting control potential that compensates for the drift, ensuring the residual potential is formed correctly.

modules.name: Variance-Controlling Guidance (VCG) Solver
modules.description: Implements the VCG algorithm which parameterizes the control drift as a linear combination of local vector bases, constructs the corresponding linear system by estimating expectations over weighted particles, and solves the small linear system to obtain the coefficients that explicitly minimize the variance of the residual potential.

modules.name: Energy-Controlling Guidance (ECG) Solver
modules.description: Implements the ECG algorithm which parameterizes the scalar control potential as a linear combination of scalar bases, constructs the linear system arising from the variational formulation of the Poisson equation, and solves it to derive the curl-free control drift that minimizes the energy functional.

modules.name: Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) Engine
modules.description: Manages the weighted particle simulation, executing the controlled SDE forward pass, updating log-weights based on the effective residual potential, tracking the Effective Sample Size (ESS), and triggering systematic resampling when ESS falls below the threshold to prevent weight collapse.

modules.name: Iterative Refinement Controller
modules.description: Implements the multi-round inference procedure where the effective drift and potential learned in one pass are accumulated into the baseline dynamics for the subsequent pass, progressively reducing variance and stabilizing the ESS across refinement rounds without external training.

modules.name: Statistical Distribution Metrics
modules.description: Calculates distributional distance metrics to evaluate sample quality, including the Negative Log-Likelihood difference, Maximum Mean Discrepancy (using Random Fourier Features for RBF kernel approximation), and Sliced Wasserstein Distance between generated and reference distributions.

modules.name: Physical & Structural Evaluation
modules.description: Evaluates the physical validity and structural accuracy of generated samples, computing Radial Distribution Functions (RDF) and Wasserstein-1 distances on energy distributions for particle systems, as well as executing PoseBusters checks (clashes, bond lengths, chirality) for protein-ligand complexes.

modules.name: Score Network Training Pipeline
modules.description: Implements the training loop for the equivariant score network using the EDM denoising objective, managing the sampling of noise levels from a log-normal distribution, optimizing the network parameters, and periodically refreshing the training dataset with newly simulated molecular configurations.

modules.name: Experiment Orchestrator & Baselines
modules.description: Coordinates the end-to-end execution of experiments across different domains (GMM, DW-4, LJ-13, Proteins), managing configurations for ablation studies (varying particle counts, annealing factors, reward strengths), and implementing baseline methods like Pure Guidance and standard Guidance-SMC for comparative analysis.
